options.text: The area of the hexagon equals the sum of the areas of those triangles.
Only a quadrilateral can be split into triangles to find area.
Any polygon can be divided into triangles, so combining those triangle areas gives the hexagon's area.
The printed label hexagon alone gives the area without combining triangle areas.

stem:
Diya has a hexagon. From one vertex she draws diagonals that split the hexagon into triangles. She wants the area of the hexagon in square centimetres.

Which two claims are correct?

teacher.key_rationale: Any polygon splits into triangles; the hexagon area is the sum of those triangle areas.
